question: My parents stay in Hougang. Is there any extra help if we buy a flat near them?

response.message: If you are applying to live with your parents/ child, you must include them in your HFE letter and flat applications. They must physically reside in the flat and their names cannot be removed during the minimum occupation period (MOP) after the flat purchase. [CHUNK_BTO_116]

citations.title: Buying a new flat (BTO/SBF): Priority Schemes > Eligibility conditions
citations.text:
- At least 1 parent/ child, married<sup>\[1\]</sup> or single (including widowed or divorced parent/ child), is a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident. The single child must be aged 35 years old and above.
- If you are applying to live with your parents/ child, you must include them in your HFE letter and flat applications. They must physically reside in the flat and their names cannot be removed during the minimum occupation period (MOP) after the flat purchase. If you or any person listed in the application owns or has an interest in any HDB flat, you must dispose of the interest in the flat, within 6 months of completing your flat purchase.
- If you are applying to live near your parents/ child, you must be applying for a flat in a project where the nearest block is within 4 km from an HDB flat, HDB rental flat, or a private residential property that your parents/ child lives in:
Property types that parents/ child lives in Condition HDB flat Your parents/ child must live in, and be the owners or registered occupiers of the flat<sup>\[3\]</sup>. If the flat is not owned by your parents/ child it must be owned and lived in by their immediate family members<sup>\[4\]</sup>.
HDB rental flat Your parents/ child must live in and be the registered tenant or occupier(s) of the flat. Private residential property Your parents/ child must own and live in the private residential property, or live in a private residential property owned and lived in by their immediate family members <sup>\[4\]</sup>. \[1\] Applicable to fiancé/ fiancée applicants.
\[2\] Also applicable to Singapore Citizens aged 35 or above who are married to a non-resident spouse.
\[3\] If your parents/ child booked an HDB flat under construction or applied to buy a resale flat, the new flat or resale flat may be used for the proximity reference.
\[4\] Immediate family members refer to child or adopted child, parent(s) or parent(s)-in-law, and/ or siblings.

related.title: Proximity Housing Grant (PHG): Proximity Housing Grant for Families Buying Resale Flats
related.text:
Find out the eligibility conditions for couples and families to apply for the Proximity Housing Grant.

If you are buying a resale flat to live with or near your parents/ child, you may apply for the following Proximity Housing Grant (PHG):

- $30,000 to live with your parents/ child
- $20,000 to live near your parents/ child (within 4km)

You may also receive the following housing grants if you meet the eligibility conditions:

- CPF Housing Grants for Resale Flats (Families)
- Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (Families)
- Step-Up CPF Housing Grant (Families)

Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter via the HDB Flat Portal for a holistic understanding of your housing and financing options before you embark on your home buying journey. It will inform you upfront of your eligibility to purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amount of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.

related.title: Using CPF for housing: Home buying guide for members below 55 > Non-mature Estates
related.text:
Bukit Batok, Bukit Panjang, Choa Chu Kang, Hougang, Jurong East, Jurong West, Punggol, Sembawang, Sengkang, Woodlands, Yishun

- Access to mature estates are prioritised for special groups such as first-timer families.
- Mature estates are generally more expensive. For example, in previous BTO exercises, the starting selling price (excluding grants) of a 3-room flat in non-mature estates such as Choa Chu Kang was more than 30% cheaper than a 3-room flat in mature estates such as Kallang. It is important to note that the prices can fluctuate over time and may be influenced by various factors such as market conditions.

If you have decided that upgrading is necessary for you, why not consider living near your children or your parents?

Besides the convenience and being surrounded by your loved ones, you also get to enjoy housing grants and schemes provided by the Government to encourage families to live closer together. These include the Proximity Housing Grant (PHG), as well as other schemes like the Multi-Generation Priority Scheme (MGPS).

There are some regions which will be benefitting from significant development over the next few years, with some already underway. Many of the non-mature estates can be found in these regions. Explore their regional highlights below.

There are exciting plans to develop these urban areas into the Punggol Digital District and the Jurong Lake District, creating vibrant communities for living and working.

More families in the North can look forward to new green and blue spaces to live, work and play at.

question: I'm single, turning 35 next year. Should I wait to buy or can I get anything now?

response.message: Single Singaporeans who are aged 35 and above can buy new 2-room Flexi flats from HDB and resale HDB flats from the open market, if they meet the eligibility conditions. [CHUNK_ELIG_01]

citations.title: Flat eligibility (citizenship, household, age): The HDB Guide for Singles
citations.text:
Eligibility conditions, grants, and priority schemes for singles looking to buy an HDB flat on their own.

Single Singaporeans who are aged 35 and above can buy new 2-room Flexi flats from HDB and resale HDB flats from the open market, if they meet the eligibility conditions. Eligible first-timer singles can also receive up to $115,000 in housing grants.

related.title: Flat eligibility (citizenship, household, age): Singles
related.text:
Buy a flat alone or with another single, as Singapore Citizens aged 35 and above.

Understand the eligibility conditions, the types of flats, CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan that you may apply for if you are a Singapore citizen who is unmarried, widowed or divorced, aged 35 and above, and are buying a flat on your own.

Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter via the HDB Flat Portal for a holistic understanding of your housing and financing options before you embark on your home buying journey. It will inform you upfront of your eligibility to buy a new or resale flat, as well as the amount of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.

If you are aged 55 and above and looking to buy a short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or a Community Care Apartment (CCA), please refer to the section on seniors.

If you intend to buy a new flat (3-room or bigger) or a resale flat with CPF Housing Grant (Families) with your parents, please refer to married couples and/ or parent(s) with child(ren).

If the information below does not apply to you \[e.g. you are an unwed parent and would like to buy a flat with your child(ren), please write to us to share your situation. We will assess and advise you on your request.

related.title: Flat eligibility (citizenship, household, age): The HDB Guide for Singles > Eligibility Conditions for Singles
related.text:
To buy an HDB flat on your own as a single, you need to meet the eligibility conditions which include:

- **Citizenship:** You must be a Singapore Citizen
- **Age:** If you are unmarried, you must be at least 35 years old
- **Property ownership**: You must not own or have an interest in any local or overseas private residential property
- **Monthly housing income ceiling:** An income ceiling may apply, depending on whether you are buying a BTO flat or resale flat, as well as the flat’s classification. If you are buying a resale flat launched before the October 2024 sales exercise or a resale Standard flat, there is no income ceiling.

Check out the full eligibility conditions for singles buying HDB flats.

All buyers must have a valid HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter before they can buy an HDB flat. Your HFE letter will tell you if you are eligible to buy a new and/ or a resale flat, as well as the grants you are eligible for. Learn more about applying for the HFE letter.

question: We like an older flat. Does the age of the flat change how much CPF we can use?

response.message: The total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase and/ or paying monthly mortgage instalments will depend on the extent the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest buyer up to the age of 95. You can get the details of a flat's lease at HDB Map. [CHUNK_LEASE_11]

citations.title: Remaining lease, CPF usage and financing for resale flats: Mode of Financing for a Resale Flat > Use of CPF savings > Conditions for use of CPF savings
citations.text:
Take note of the following conditions for using your CPF savings:

- There is a limit on the total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase. Once that limit is reached, you will not be able to withdraw more of your CPF savings and have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash
- The total amount of CPF savings that can be used for your flat purchase and/ or paying monthly mortgage instalments will depend on the extent the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest buyer up to the age of 95. You can get the details of a flat's lease at HDB Map. Details on the use of CPF savings and the applicable limits are shown in the table below:
Remaining lease of flat is at least 20 years and can cover the youngest buyer up to the age of 95 Applicable Limits for CPF Usage Yes The amount use is capped at the **lower** of the value of flat or price of the flat at the time of purchase.No The amount is pro-rated based on the extent the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest buyer up to the age of 95. When the allowed CPF amount is used up, buyers have to pay the balance flat purchase price and/ or monthly mortgage instalments in cash. This will help buyers to set aside CPF savings for their housing needs during retirement (e.g. buying a replacement property).

related.title: HDB housing loan and bank loans: Housing Loan from HDB > Use of CPF savings
related.text:
Find out the requirements on the use of CPF savings for your flat purchase and for paying the monthly instalments.

Applicants have the option to:

- Retain up to $20,000 of the available savings in each of their CPF Ordinary Account (OA)
- Use the savings in their CPF OA to pay the stamp fee, registration fee, legal fees, and premium for the CPF Home Protection Insurance (if applicable)

The remaining balance in your CPF OA must be used to pay for the flat purchase or take over ownership of an existing flat, before the HDB housing loan can be granted.

The total amount of CPF savings that can be used to buy or take over the flat and pay the monthly mortgage instalments will depend on:

- Extent that the remaining lease of the flat can cover the youngest applicant up to the age of 95; and

When the allowed CPF amount is used up, you have to pay for the balance purchase price and/ or the monthly mortgage instalments in cash. For more information on the use of CPF savings, you may use CPF Board’s calculator.

Occupier(s) cannot use their CPF OA savings or housing grant for the flat purchase or servicing of housing loan.

related.title: Using CPF for housing: Home buying guide for members above 55
related.text:
Consider using a mix of cash and CPF to pay for the purchase price and loan (if eligible). Every dollar less you spend from your CPF account on your home is at least a dollar more for your retirement.

If you qualify for a loan and intend to use CPF, keep your monthly instalments within your Ordinary Account contribution. Consider keeping 6 months of your monthly instalment in your Ordinary Account as a buffer.

CPF savings can be used for the purchase price, housing loan, stamp and legal fees.

If you are aged 55 and above and selling your current flat, the CPF refunds will first be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Full Retirement Sum. The remaining refunds will be retained in your Ordinary Account.

You can check the amount available for use on your Home ownership dashboard, including the exact amount that you would need to refund to your CPF account upon the sale of your current flat that can be reused for your next flat.

If you are buying a resale flat, use our **Housing Usage Calculator** to estimate the amount of CPF savings you may use based on the flat's remaining lease.

Apply for an HDB Flat Eligibility (HFE) letter to find out if you can purchase a new or resale flat, as well as the amounts of CPF housing grants and HDB housing loan you are eligible for.

Note that if you are buying a short-lease flat, such as a 2-room Flexi flat or a Community Care Apartment, you are not eligible for housing loans.

You can book an appointment to visit an HDB Branch. You may also wish to contact HDB via their Write to Us.
